title: One-Stop Pilot Program Extension Act

claims.claim: Rewrites subsection (d) of section 7132 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263; 49 U.S.C. 44901 note).
claims.sourceSpan: Subsection (d) of section 7132 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263; 49 U.S.C. 44901 note) is amended to read as follows

claims.claim: The TSA Administrator, in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, may permit checked baggage arriving from participating foreign last point of departure airports to continue on additional flights originating in the United States without additional TSA re-screening.
claims.sourceSpan: the Administrator, in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), may permit checked baggage arriving on direct flights or flight segments arriving from participating foreign last point of departure airports referred to in subsection (b) to continue on additional flights or flight segments originating in the United States without additional TSA security
claims.note: Source says 'the Administrator'; 'TSA Administrator' is grounded by the same clause's 'without additional TSA security re-screening'. Permissive 'may permit' preserved (no direction inversion).

claims.claim: if four conditions are met
claims.sourceSpan: if the following requirements are satisfied
claims.note: Four enumerated requirements (1)-(4), conjunctive.

claims.claim: Subsection (b) also amends subsection (k) of section 7132 by striking "six" and inserting "ten".
claims.sourceSpan: Subsection (k) of section 7132 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 is amended by striking ``six'' and inserting ``ten''

claims.claim: extending the associated authority
claims.sourceSpan: (b) Extension
claims.note: The six->ten change is framed as an 'extension'; grounded in the bill's own subsection heading '(b) Extension' and the short title 'Extension Act'. Bill does not state what (k) governs, so the characterization stays deliberately vague.

claims.claim: Rewrites section 7132(d) of the FY2023 NDAA to let TSA and CBP allow checked-baggage transfers from participating foreign airports to continue without re-screening on U.S. connecting flights when four conditions are met.
claims.sourceSpan: the Administrator, in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), may permit checked baggage arriving on direct flights or flight segments arriving from participating foreign last point of departure airports referred to in subsection (b) to continue on additional flights or flight segments originating in the United States without additional TSA security
claims.note: 'connecting flights' glosses 'additional flights or flight segments originating in the United States'; faithful.

claims.claim: changes "six" to "ten" in subsection (k)
claims.sourceSpan: striking ``six'' and inserting ``ten''

claims.claim: Rewritten Checked-Baggage Re-Screening Rule
claims.sourceSpan: (d) Re-Screening of Checked Baggage
claims.note: 'Rewritten' grounded in 'is amended to read as follows'; heading matches.

claims.claim: Amends 49 U.S.C. 44901 note (section 7132(d) of the FY2023 NDAA, Public Law 117-263)
claims.sourceSpan: Subsection (d) of section 7132 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263; 49 U.S.C. 44901 note) is amended to read as follows

claims.claim: TSA Administrator, in coordination with the CBP Commissioner, may permit continuation without additional TSA re-screening
claims.sourceSpan: the Administrator, in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), may permit checked baggage arriving on direct flights or flight segments arriving from participating foreign last point of departure airports referred to in subsection (b) to continue on additional flights or flight segments originating in the United States without additional TSA security

claims.claim: Four Conditions Must Be Met
claims.sourceSpan: if the following requirements are satisfied
claims.note: Conjunctive requirements (1)-(4).

claims.claim: Initial checked baggage screening at the foreign airport used an explosives detection system under an aviation security screening agreement described in subsection (e)
claims.sourceSpan: The initial checked baggage screening at such an airport was conducted using an explosives detection system in accordance with an aviation security screening agreement described in subsection (e)

claims.claim: Passengers cannot access their checked baggage until arrival at their final destination
claims.sourceSpan: Passengers arriving from such airports are unable to access their checked baggage until arrival at their final destination
claims.note: 'cannot access' = 'unable to access'.

claims.claim: CBP has received timely images meeting CBP requirements before U.S. arrival
claims.sourceSpan: CBP has received timely images of such baggage prior to the arrival in the United States of such passengers and baggage that satisfy CBP requirements from such an airport corresponding to the checked baggage of such passengers to ensure appropriate border security enforcement can be completed in an efficient manner

claims.claim: CBP has not identified any such passenger or baggage for further inspection
claims.sourceSpan: CBP has not identified any such passenger or baggage for further inspection

claims.claim: Extension — "six" to "ten"
claims.sourceSpan: (b) Extension
claims.note: Extension heading + six->ten both in source.

claims.claim: Amends section 7132(k) of the FY2023 NDAA by striking "six" and inserting "ten"
claims.sourceSpan: Subsection (k) of section 7132 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 is amended by striking ``six'' and inserting ``ten''

claims.claim: Names the Act the "One-Stop Pilot Program Extension Act."
claims.sourceSpan: One-Stop Pilot Program Extension Act

claims.claim: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the ``One-Stop Pilot Program Extension
claims.note: Section is a pure citation clause; no operative effect.

claims.claim: Section 2 — One-Stop Program
claims.sourceSpan: SEC. 2. ONE-STOP PROGRAM.

claims.claim: Subsection (a) amends subsection (d) of section 7132, subject to subsection (f), so the TSA Administrator, in coordination with the CBP Commissioner, may permit checked baggage arriving on direct flights or flight segments arriving from participating foreign last point of departure airports (referred to in subsection (b)) to continue on additional flights or flight segments originating in the United States without additional TSA security re-screening if four conditions are satisfied.
claims.sourceSpan: the Administrator, in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), may permit checked baggage arriving on direct flights or flight segments arriving from participating foreign last point of departure airports referred to in subsection (b) to continue on additional flights or flight segments originating in the United States without additional TSA security
claims.note: Bill SEC 2(a) heading is '(a) Checked Baggage Re-Screening'; it amends statute 7132(d). Cross-reference '(referred to in subsection (b))' matches source 'referred to in subsection (b)'.

claims.claim: The rewrite retains the subsection heading ("Re-Screening of Checked Baggage").
claims.sourceSpan: is amended to read as follows
claims.note: The new (d) does carry the heading 'Re-Screening of Checked Baggage', but 'retains' asserts continuity with the pre-amendment (d), whose text is not in the source (only the replacement is shown). Cannot confirm the heading is unchanged. Low impact.

claims.claim: The rewrite retains the subject-to-(f) limitation.
claims.sourceSpan: Subject to subsection (f)

claims.claim: ...while restructuring the substantive conditions.
claims.sourceSpan: is amended to read as follows
claims.note: 'Amended to read as follows' establishes a wholesale rewrite of the prior (d); 'restructuring' is grounded even though the prior conditions are not shown.

claims.claim: Condition (1): initial checked baggage screening at the foreign airport was conducted using an explosives detection system in accordance with an aviation security screening agreement described in subsection (e).
claims.sourceSpan: The initial checked baggage screening at such an airport was conducted using an explosives detection system in accordance with an aviation security screening agreement described in subsection (e)

claims.claim: Condition (2): passengers arriving from such airports cannot access their checked baggage until arrival at their final destination.
claims.sourceSpan: Passengers arriving from such airports are unable to access their checked baggage until arrival at their final destination

claims.claim: Condition (3): CBP has received timely images of the baggage prior to arrival in the United States that satisfy CBP requirements, corresponding to the checked baggage, to ensure appropriate border security enforcement can be completed in an efficient manner.
claims.sourceSpan: CBP has received timely images of such baggage prior to the arrival in the United States of such passengers and baggage that satisfy CBP requirements from such an airport corresponding to the checked baggage of such passengers to ensure appropriate border security enforcement can be completed in an efficient manner

claims.claim: Condition (4): CBP has not identified any such passenger or baggage for further inspection.
claims.sourceSpan: CBP has not identified any such passenger or baggage for further inspection

claims.claim: All four conditions must be met.
claims.sourceSpan: if the following requirements are satisfied
claims.note: Conjunctive list (1)-(4).

claims.claim: The coordination with CBP is baked into the granting authority.
claims.sourceSpan: in coordination with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP)

claims.claim: ...further reinforced by the CBP-specific conditions in paragraphs (3) and (4).
claims.sourceSpan: CBP has not identified any such passenger or baggage for further inspection
claims.note: Paragraphs (3) and (4) both name CBP; accurate characterization.

claims.claim: Subsection (b) amends subsection (k) of section 7132 of the FY2023 NDAA by striking "six" and inserting "ten."
claims.sourceSpan: Subsection (k) of section 7132 of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 is amended by striking ``six'' and inserting ``ten''

claims.claim: Subsection (k) is not otherwise reproduced in this Act; the change is a single numeric substitution.
claims.sourceSpan: amended by striking ``six'' and inserting ``ten''
claims.note: Source shows only the strike/insert; (k)'s content is not reproduced.

claims.claim: The bill does not restate what subsection (k) of section 7132 measures (the "six" being changed to "ten"), so the practical effect of that change is not visible in the Act's own text.
claims.sourceSpan: amended by striking ``six'' and inserting ``ten''
claims.note: Accurate statement of absence: source shows the substitution but never states what (k) governs.

claims.claim: The bill does not authorize funding for TSA or CBP implementation.
claims.note: Accurate absence: no appropriation or funding provision anywhere in the source text.

claims.claim: The bill does not describe how the aviation security screening agreements in subsection (e) are negotiated or approved.
claims.sourceSpan: in accordance with an aviation security screening agreement described in subsection (e)
claims.note: Accurate absence: source only cross-references the (e) agreement; no negotiation/approval process is stated in the text provided.

claims.claim: The bill does not require public reporting on which foreign airports participate or how often the no-re-screening authority is used.
claims.note: Accurate absence: no reporting or transparency provision in the source text.
